idea: Chan, Jegadeesh and Lakonishok (1996): prices absorb analyst estimate revisions slowly, so stocks with recent upward revisions keep outperforming.
rationale_data: analyst_revision_score_5d_medium (multi-horizon analyst revision signals, model category): the average analyst revision score over the last five days.
rationale_operators: rank() normalises the score across stocks; industry neutralization compares revisions within industries.

idea: Revision breadth: a revision backed by many analysts moving in the same direction carries more information than the average change (Chan, Jegadeesh and Lakonishok 1996).
rationale_data: Counts of analysts raising and lowering FY1 EPS estimates over the past 14 days (multi-horizon analyst revision signals, model category).
rationale_operators: The difference is net revision breadth; rank() normalises it; industry neutralization removes industry-wide revision waves.

idea: Womack (1996) and Jegadeesh, Kim, Krische and Lee (2004): prices keep drifting for weeks after analyst recommendation changes.
rationale_data: recommendation_change_component_short (multi-horizon analyst revision signals, model category): the recommendation-change component of the revision score, short horizon.
rationale_operators: rank() normalises the component; industry neutralization compares within industries.

idea: Post-earnings-announcement drift (Bernard and Thomas 1989): prices under-react to earnings surprises, measured here against the accuracy-weighted SmartEstimate rather than the plain consensus.
rationale_data: actual_vs_predicted_surprise_pct_annual_earnings_long (multi-horizon analyst revision signals, model category): percentage difference between actual and predicted annual earnings.
rationale_operators: rank() normalises the surprise across stocks; industry neutralization removes industry earnings cycles.

idea: Gu, Kelly and Xiu (2020): combinations of many firm characteristics forecast the cross-section of returns; this vendor model forecasts excess return relative to a benchmark.
rationale_data: alpha_excess_return_forecast (AI equity alpha forecasts, model category), a vector field aggregated per stock.
rationale_operators: vec_avg() aggregates the vector values; rank() normalises; subindustry neutralization removes industry bets.

idea: Changes in analyst sentiment predict returns because recommendation and estimate changes diffuse slowly (Jegadeesh et al. 2004).
rationale_data: analyst_sentiment_shift_score (AI equity alpha forecasts, model category): recent changes in analyst sentiment or recommendations.
rationale_operators: vec_avg() aggregates the vector field; rank() normalises it; industry neutralization compares within industries.

idea: Bernard and Thomas (1989): firms with a history of positive earnings surprises keep outperforming as investors under-react to earnings news.
rationale_data: historic_earnings_surprise_score (AI equity alpha forecasts, model category): past earnings results versus expectations.
rationale_operators: vec_avg() aggregates the vector field; rank() normalises; industry neutralization removes industry effects.

idea: Analyst-based return forecasts: revisions, dispersion and surprises jointly predict the next quarter's return (Gu, Kelly and Xiu 2020 on combining predictors).
rationale_data: analyst_60d_regression_pred (multi factor market return predictions, model category): a regression forecast of the 60-day return from analyst features.
rationale_operators: rank() keeps the ordering of the forecast; subindustry neutralization removes industry bets.

idea: Heston and Sadka (2008): stocks tend to earn similar relative returns in the same calendar months year after year; this forecast adjusts a medium-term return model for that seasonality.
rationale_data: mid_term_seasonal_adjusted_return_forecast_60d (multi factor market return predictions, model category).
rationale_operators: rank() normalises the forecast; subindustry neutralization removes industry seasonality.

idea: Option-implied information predicts stock returns (Cremers and Weinbaum 2010; An et al. 2014); a high predicted probability of a bottom-quantile 20-day return is a short signal.
rationale_data: option_quantile5_20d_pred (multi-source market return prediction, model category): predicted probability that the 20-day return falls in the 5th quantile, from option features.
rationale_operators: rank() normalises the probability and the minus sign shorts the stocks most likely to fall; industry neutralization removes industry effects.

idea: Givoly and Lakonishok (1979); Chan, Jegadeesh and Lakonishok (1996): the size of consensus EPS revisions predicts returns over the following months.
rationale_data: eps_revision_magnitude (global analyst factor signals, analyst category): scaled magnitude of FY1 EPS revisions.
rationale_operators: rank() normalises the revision magnitude; industry neutralization compares within industries.

idea: Diether, Malloy and Scherbina (2002): stocks with high dispersion in analyst forecasts earn lower future returns.
rationale_data: eps_q1_estimate_coeff_var (global analyst factor signals, analyst category): coefficient of variation of Q1 EPS estimates.
rationale_operators: rank() normalises the dispersion and the minus sign shorts high-disagreement stocks; industry neutralization removes industry effects.

idea: Expected profitability changes predict returns (Fama and French 2006; Hou, Xue and Zhang 2015, q-factor model: expected investment and profitability drive the cross-section).
rationale_data: anl82_netq_deltaprofitability_profitability2 (analyst estimate prediction data, analyst category): a profitability measure based on the predicted change of quarterly net income.
rationale_operators: rank() normalises the measure across stocks; industry neutralization compares within industries.

idea: Technical-indicator models forecast short-horizon returns (Brock, Lakonishok and LeBaron 1992; Jiang, Kelly and Xiu 2023); this is the model confidence for indicator set 10's 10-day forecast.
rationale_data: tcm_10r5_d1_prob (technical indicator chart prediction, model category).
rationale_operators: rank() normalises the score; subindustry neutralization removes industry effects.

idea: Frankel and Lee (1998), Accounting valuation, market expectation, and cross-sectional stock returns: stocks priced low relative to residual-income intrinsic value outperform.
rationale_data: price_to_intrinsic_value_industry_rank_3 (predictive StarMine signal set, model category): industry percentile of price to intrinsic value.
rationale_operators: rank() normalises it and the minus sign buys stocks cheap relative to intrinsic value; industry neutralization keeps the comparison within industries.

idea: Gu, Kelly and Xiu (2020): machine-learning composites of firm characteristics forecast relative returns; this vendor score ranks securities by forecast return.
rationale_data: alpha_score (AI equity alpha forecasts, model category), a vector field aggregated per stock.
rationale_operators: vec_avg() aggregates the vector values; rank() normalises; subindustry neutralization removes industry bets.
